learn: Hola means hello at any time of day. Buenos días is good morning, buenas tardes is good afternoon and buenas noches is good evening or good night.
Hasta luego means see you later. Hasta mañana means see you tomorrow.
Many people greet each other with a handshake or a hug.
check: What do you say in the afternoon?
lessons.try: Use the right greeting each time you see your family today.

learn: ¿Cómo estás? means how are you? It is for a friend or someone your age.
Answers: estoy bien (I am fine), estoy muy bien (I am very well), más o menos (so-so).
After you answer, be polite and ask back: ¿y tú? (and you?).
lessons.try: Practice a talk with a partner: ¿cómo estás? Estoy bien, ¿y tú?

learn: Por favor means please. Gracias means thank you. De nada means you are welcome.
Perdón or disculpa means excuse me or sorry.
Lo siento means I am sorry when you have made a mistake.
lessons.try: Use por favor, gracias and lo siento in a puppet show.

learn: Tú is for friends and family.
Usted is polite, for grown-ups you don't know well.
check: To a grown-up you say ¿Cómo ___ usted?
lessons.try: Greet a friend and a pretend principal.

learn: Perdón or disculpe means excuse me.
Con permiso: excuse me, may I pass?
check: Con permiso is said when you want to...
lessons.try: Practise walking past with "con permiso".

learn: Bienvenido or bienvenida to one person.
check: A welcome sign for visitors says...
lessons.try: Make a "Bienvenidos" sign for the door.

learn: Answer the phone: ¿Bueno? (Mexico) or ¿Aló? or ¿Diga? (other places).
Say who you are: Habla Ana.
check: In Mexico people answer the phone with...
lessons.try: Role-play a pretend phone call.

learn: ¿Me das el lápiz, por favor? (Can you give me the pencil, please?)
Answer: Sí, aquí tienes (Yes, here you are).
lessons.try: Trade classroom things politely.
Polite words skit.

learn: Uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco, seis, siete, ocho, nueve, diez.
Write the numeral and say the word for each number.
Practice counting objects, not just saying the words.
lessons.try: Count ten crayons in Spanish, touching each one.

learn: These numbers each have their own special word.
Quince sounds a little like cinco, because it is ten and five.
lessons.try: Make 11 to 15 with blocks and say each number.

learn: Dieciséis means ten and six: diez y seis joined together.
lessons.try: Count your fingers and toes in Spanish. You should reach veinte!

learn: ¿Cuántos niños hay? How many children are there?
Hay means there is or there are.
lessons.try: Count classmates in Spanish.

learn: Only tell your number to trusted people.
check: Tell your real number only to...
lessons.try: Say a pretend phone number in Spanish.
Solve five sums out loud.
Solve take-away stories with counters.

learn: Lotería is a picture bingo game.
lessons.try: Play number lotería to 20.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Numbers to 20
lessons.try: Number relay race.

learn: Rojo, azul, amarillo, verde, naranja, morado, rosa, blanco, negro, café, gris.
Gris means gray, like a cloud on a rainy day.
In Spanish the color comes after the thing: un carro rojo means a red car.
check: In Spanish the color usually goes...
lessons.try: Name the colors of five things you are wearing or can see.

learn: El círculo is a circle. El cuadrado is a square. El triángulo is a triangle.
El rectángulo is a rectangle. La estrella is a star. El corazón is a heart.
A wheel is a círculo. A slice of pizza can be a triángulo.
check: How many sides does a triángulo have?
lessons.try: Go on a shape hunt and find a círculo, a cuadrado and a triángulo.

learn: Un círculo azul is a blue circle. Un cuadrado verde is a green square.
Ask ¿qué es? (what is it?) and answer es un... (it is a...).
Big is grande. Small is pequeño.
lessons.try: Draw un triángulo rojo grande and un círculo amarillo pequeño.

learn: Colour words go after the noun: un círculo rojo.
check: Un círculo grande is a big...
In Spanish, colour words usually come ___ the noun.
Un cuadrado pequeño is a small...
lessons.try: Describe five shapes by size and colour.
Draw a star, heart and oval and label them.
Hunt for shapes and say them in Spanish.

learn: Make a house: un cuadrado y un triángulo.
Make a sun: un círculo amarillo.
lessons.try: Build a picture from paper shapes.

check: Verde, verde, amarillo, verde, verde... next is
lessons.try: Make a bead pattern and say it.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Colours and Shapes
lessons.try: Shape and colour bingo.

learn: El lápiz is the pencil. El libro is the book. El papel is the paper.
La mesa is the table. La silla is the chair. La mochila is the backpack.
El maestro or la maestra is the teacher.
lessons.try: Label five things in your room with paper tags in Spanish.

learn: Teachers say siéntense (sit down), levántense (stand up) and escuchen (listen).
Miren means look. Repitan means repeat.
Silencio, por favor means quiet, please.
lessons.try: Play Simón dice (Simon says) with these commands.

learn: Necesito means I need. Necesito un lápiz means I need a pencil.
¿Puedo ir al baño? means may I go to the bathroom?
Add por favor to sound polite.
lessons.try: Practice asking for a pencil and a book in Spanish.

learn: El lápiz (pencil), la goma (eraser), las tijeras (scissors).
lessons.try: Label supplies on your desk.

learn: ¿Dónde está el libro? Where is the book?
Está en la mesa: it's on the table.
lessons.try: Hide and find classroom things.
Make a school map in Spanish.

learn: El director or la directora: principal.
check: The principal is el director or la...
lessons.try: Draw a school helper and label them.

learn: Escucha (listen), levanta la mano (raise your hand).
lessons.try: Write three rules in Spanish.
Classroom scavenger hunt.

learn: Mi familia means my family. Mi mamá, mi papá, mi hermano, mi hermana.
Tengo means I have. Tengo un hermano means I have a brother.
Los abuelos are grandparents. El tío is uncle and la tía is aunt.
lessons.try: Tell a partner about your family using tengo.

learn: La mascota means the pet. ¿Tienes una mascota? means do you have a pet?
El conejo is the rabbit. El hámster is the hamster. La tortuga is the turtle.
If you have no pet, you can say no tengo mascota.
check: I do not have a pet
lessons.try: Draw a real or dream pet and name it in Spanish.

learn: Grande means big and pequeño means small.
Bonito means pretty or nice. Rápido means fast. Lento means slow.
Mi perro es grande means my dog is big.
lessons.try: Say two things about an animal: es pequeño, es rápido...
Draw a family tree with Spanish labels.

check: Tengo dos hermanos means I have ___ siblings.
lessons.try: Survey classmates about siblings.

learn: Doy de comer a mi perro: I feed my dog.
Paseo a mi perro: I walk my dog.
check: Paseo a mi perro means I ___ my dog.
lessons.try: Make a pet care chart.

check: ¿Cómo se llama tu gato? asks the cat's...
Mi perro se llama Max means my dog is called...
lessons.try: Ask a friend their pet's name.

check: Mi mamá es alta means my mum is...
lessons.try: Write a sentence about a family member.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Family and Pets
lessons.try: Present your family and pets.

learn: La camisa is the shirt. Los pantalones are the pants. Los zapatos are the shoes.
El sombrero is the hat. La chaqueta is the jacket. Los calcetines are socks.
Llevo means I am wearing. Llevo una camisa azul.
lessons.try: Tell someone what you are wearing using llevo.

learn: ¿Qué tiempo hace? means what is the weather like?
Hace sol means it is sunny. Hace calor means it is hot. Hace frío means it is cold.
Llueve means it is raining. Nieva means it is snowing.
check: What is the weather like in a desert summer?
lessons.try: Look outside each morning this week and say the weather in Spanish.

learn: When hace frío, we wear una chaqueta.
When llueve, we use un paraguas, an umbrella.
When hace calor, we wear a hat and drink agua.
check: When hace calor you should drink...
lessons.try: Pick clothes for a cold day and a hot day, naming them in Spanish.

check: Una camisa azul is a blue...
lessons.try: Describe your outfit in Spanish.
Draw the four seasons.

learn: Hoy hace sol: today it's sunny.
lessons.try: Be the class weather reporter.
Act out hot and cold.

learn: For the beach: traje de baño, gorra.
lessons.try: Pack a pretend suitcase in Spanish.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Clothes and Weather
lessons.try: Weather and clothes matching game.

learn: La fresa is the strawberry. La sandía is the watermelon. La piña is the pineapple.
El mango is a mango. La pera is a pear.
Many fruits grow in warm places like Mexico.
lessons.try: Make a fruit salad and name each fruit in Spanish.

learn: El desayuno is breakfast. El almuerzo is lunch. La cena is dinner.
Huevos are eggs. Cereal is cereal. Pollo is chicken.
Quiero means I want. Quiero huevos, por favor.
lessons.try: Say what you want for breakfast tomorrow using quiero.

learn: Delicioso means delicious. Rico also means tasty.
Dulce means sweet. Salado means salty.
Me gusta and no me gusta tell what you like.
lessons.try: Taste three foods and say dulce or salado for each.
Draw a salad and label it.
Set a pretend table and name each thing.
Role-play a taco stand.
Taste or draw a dish from one country.

check: Frutas y verduras means fruits and...
lessons.try: Draw a healthy plate in Spanish.
Restaurant role-play.

learn: Sábado is Saturday and domingo is Sunday.
In Spanish the days do not start with a capital letter.
check: Days of the week in Spanish start with...
lessons.try: Say the days in order every morning this week.

learn: Hoy means today. Mañana means tomorrow. Ayer means yesterday.
¿Qué día es hoy? means what day is today?
Hoy es lunes means today is Monday.
lessons.try: Answer ¿qué día es hoy? every morning.

learn: Some days are school days. El fin de semana is the weekend: sábado and domingo.
You can say el lunes voy a la escuela, on Monday I go to school.
A calendar helps us plan the week.
lessons.try: Make a week chart and draw one activity for each day, labeling the day in Spanish.

learn: Twelve months, written with small letters.
check: Months in Spanish are written with ___ letters.
lessons.try: Make a birthday month chart.

learn: Hoy es lunes, mañana es martes.
check: If hoy es lunes, mañana es...
lessons.try: Say ayer, hoy and mañana each morning.

learn: Hoy es el cinco de mayo.
check: El cinco de mayo is the fifth of...
The date uses number, de, and...
lessons.try: Write today's date in Spanish.

learn: El domingo visito a mi abuela.
lessons.try: Tell a partner your weekend plan.

learn: Sing the days of the week song.
lessons.try: Sing and clap the days.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Days and Months
lessons.try: Calendar quiz.

learn: La granja is the farm. La selva is the jungle. El mar is the sea. El desierto is the desert.
La vaca vive en la granja. The cow lives on the farm.
lessons.try: Sort animal pictures into granja, selva, mar and desierto.

learn: In the Sonoran Desert live el coyote, la serpiente (snake) and el correcaminos (roadrunner).
La lagartija is a lizard. El búho is an owl.
Desert animals are good at staying cool and finding water.
lessons.try: Draw a desert animal and label it in Spanish.

learn: Corre means runs. Salta means jumps. Nada means swims. Vuela means flies.
El pájaro vuela. El pez nada. El conejo salta.
Can you act out each word?
lessons.try: A grown-up calls out corre, salta, nada or vuela, and you act it out.

learn: Many live in Central and South America.
lessons.try: Draw a jungle with three animals.
Make an ocean mural.
Act out farm animals.
Go on a bug hunt and name them.
Describe three animals.
Habitat sorting game.

learn: Día de los Muertos is a Mexican celebration on November 1 and 2 to remember family members who have died.
Families make an altar, called an ofrenda, with photos, flowers called cempasúchil, and favorite foods.
It is a happy, colorful time to remember and love.
check: Día de los Muertos comes from...
lessons.try: Draw a marigold flower and talk about someone you remember.

lessons.t: Las Posadas and the New Year
learn: Las Posadas is a December celebration with songs, candles and a walk from house to house.
On New Year's Eve, some families eat twelve grapes at midnight, one for each month.
¡Feliz Año Nuevo! means Happy New Year!
check: How many grapes for New Year?
lessons.try: Count twelve grapes (or other fruit) in Spanish.

learn: You have learned greetings, numbers, colors, family, food, clothes and days.
Put them together: hola, me llamo..., tengo seis años (I am six years old).
lessons.try: Give a one-minute talk in Spanish about yourself to your family.

learn: Remembers a battle won in Puebla, Mexico, in 1862.
It is not Mexico's Independence Day.
check: Cinco de Mayo remembers a battle in...
lessons.try: Find Puebla on a map.

learn: September 15 to October 15 in the US.
check: Hispanic Heritage Month starts on September...
lessons.try: Make a poster about one famous person.
Design a carnaval mask.
Make a birthday card in Spanish.

learn: La gallinita ciega: like blind man's buff.
Doña Blanca: a circle game with a song.
lessons.try: Play a traditional circle game.
Perform in the class Spanish show.
